plan.intended_use: <Who uses the product, for what decision, and what stays in Orcanos as the system of record.>
plan.validation_not_verification: Verification asks “was the software built to its specification?” — the developer's unit, integration and automated end-to-end tests answer it, and they are not repeated here. Validation asks “does it meet the user's need in real use?” Every test in this package is therefore run through the normal user interface, on a production-equivalent installation connected to a real Orcanos account, against a defined test data set, and its result is checked against Orcanos itself as the independent source of truth.
plan.base_system_reliance: Orcanos ALM / QMS is covered by its own validation package, including most 21 CFR Part 11 controls: user identity and passwords, electronic signatures, the record audit trail, workflow enforcement, record retention and permissions. This package relies on that work and does not re-test it. It tests that the add-on uses those functions correctly in the user's workflow, and it assesses the few records the add-on keeps itself (section 4).
plan.approach: Risk-based, following FDA Computer Software Assurance and GAMP 5 (2nd ed.). The add-on is used as evidence in design reviews and audits (21 CFR 820 / QMSR, ISO 13485 §4.1.6 and §7.3), so the failure that matters most is a result that looks right but is not — a missing trace shown as present, an unflagged gap, an incomplete export. Each user requirement carries a risk level that sets how it is tested.

risk_levels.meaning: A wrong result could be relied on as compliance evidence without being noticed.
risk_levels.assurance: Scripted, automated test; every step with expected result and screenshot; result compared against Orcanos through its API; produced files kept.

risk_levels.meaning: A failure is visible to the user, or is backed by a validated Orcanos control.
risk_levels.assurance: Scripted, automated test with expected results and a screenshot per step.

risk_levels.meaning: Convenience function; no effect on a record or a decision.
risk_levels.assurance: Unscripted / exploratory testing, summarised in the report.

plan.automation: Every validation test is automated with Playwright: a real browser drives the real user interface exactly as a user would, on a production-equivalent installation connected to a real Orcanos account. Expected results are checked against Orcanos through its own API, by test code that is independent of the add-on's code. Automation is only the execution method — the tests stay validation tests: they follow the intended use end to end, from the user's side, not internal units. Each step stores a screenshot; produced files and the Orcanos data used for comparison are kept with the run. A person reviews the evidence and approves the test report.
execution_rules: Tests run in the order of the protocol (STD); later tests use the panel created by VT-005.
Every run gets its own results folder (results.json + evidence). Results are never edited by hand; the test report prints the SHA-256 of results.json.
A test passes only if every one of its steps was checked and passed. A test that cannot start because a prerequisite is missing is Blocked, never Pass.
A failed or blocked test needs a deviation record — description, impact on the requirement, resolution — before the report is approved. A re-run after a fix creates a new run.
Long real-time tests (the 45-minute idle time-out) run only when explicitly included; the report shows them as Not run otherwise.
The person approving the report must not be the developer of the feature under test.

roles.duty: Owns this package; keeps URS, SRS and STD in step with the product; prepares the test data set.
Starts the automated run on the validation environment; reviews the screenshots and files of every step; raises deviations.
Reviews the package and the evidence; confirms deviations are resolved.
Approves the plan before execution and the report after it.

part11.intro: 21 CFR Part 11 applies to electronic records and signatures kept under FDA predicate rules. Most of its controls are provided by Orcanos ALM / QMS and are covered by the Orcanos validation package; they are marked “Base”. The product is assessed for what it adds: <list the records it keeps itself, and whether it applies e-signatures>.
part11.legend: Base = met by Orcanos, covered by its validation · Met = met by the add-on, evidence cited · Partial = met in part, open item named · Gap = not met, open item · NA = not applicable.

ai.intro: Some modules offer AI assistance. AI is opt-in per account and off unless licensed. In every case the model proposes and a person decides: no AI output becomes an Orcanos record without explicit human confirmation.

features.control: <the human step before anything becomes a record>

controls: Opt-in per account; hidden for accounts not licensed, and in a region where the AI service is not yet hosted locally.
The engine is chosen per account (Anthropic directly, or the Orcanos AWS Bedrock gateway).
The model has no tools: it cannot call Orcanos, the database or the network. It sees only the current account's data for the one request.
No credentials are ever placed in a prompt.
House-style prompts can be changed only by the account administrator.
Every model call is metered and costed per account.
ai.validation: AI output is not deterministic, so its content is not validated as correct. What is validated is the control around it: (1) nothing reaches Orcanos without explicit human confirmation; (2) AI content is labelled as such; (3) AI is unavailable to accounts that are not licensed; (4) the model receives only the data stated above. These become user requirements in the AI increment of this package. The approach follows GAMP 5 (2nd ed.) Appendix D11 and FDA Computer Software Assurance.

security.intro: The full control list, with open gaps, is maintained in <docs/SECURITY_CONTROLS.md>. The summary below is the part relevant to validation.

data_integrity.intro: ALCOA+ as it applies to an add-on whose records are, almost entirely, Orcanos's.

rows.how: Every read and write to Orcanos is made with the user's own login — never a shared or service account — so Orcanos attributes it to that person.
Exports are human-readable HTML and Excel; the Doc Review record is a PDF.
Data is read live from Orcanos; a cached view says it is cached and when it was taken; ⟳ refresh re-reads Orcanos (VT-007).
Orcanos holds the original record; the add-on holds caches and copies only, apart from its own records listed in section 4.
Matrix content and gap flags are validated against Orcanos (URS-020, URS-021).
Exports cover every page and level (URS-050).
One time base: every time the add-on records is UTC and labelled as such; Orcanos dates are shown exactly as Orcanos holds them.
Orcanos retention for its records; the add-on's own records on an encrypted, replicated volume with a tested restore procedure.
